A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TabMGP research. All 36 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison. Retained material can be matched across reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original coverage experiments across 11 synthetic and 19 real-data setups, alongside convergence diagnostics, posterior-density plots, and marginal-interval results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds semi-synthetic evaluations, alternative-baseline results, and further convergence and sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: Both versions use Bayesian-bootstrap covariates, sequential TabPFN response sampling, and loss minimization over completed rollouts. v3 corrects Algorithm 1's conditioning indices and explicitly initializes each rollout, matching the growing-context procedure already described in v2's Figure 1 and text.

E1.justification: Appendix G adds Concrete and Phoneme semi-synthetic scenarios combining real covariates with fitted nonlinear MLP response mechanisms. This extends the represented data-generating conditions within the existing regression and classification tasks; the original 30 setups remain.

E2.justification: New Tables 6–7 substantially broaden the comparisons with Bayes under a diffuse N(0, 10²) prior and a TabPFN-initialized copula method adapted from Nagler and Rügamer. The original Hessian-prior Bayes and standard Copula are retained. Neither copula variant is evaluated on the multinomial setups.

E3.justification: The original experimental settings remain unchanged. Supplementary protocols add empirical-covariate resampling with MLP-generated responses, longer convergence runs, and sensitivity tests varying T=N−n from 100 to 1000 while holding observed sample size fixed. These additions do not establish reruns of the retained main tables.

E4.justification: Appendices F and I substantially expand convergence validation: Figure 7 extends slow-converging rollouts, Figure 8 tests sensitivity to the observed dataset, and Figure 9 measures coverage and credible-set size across rollout lengths. These analyses expose unstable trajectories and residual sensitivity beyond v2's single-dataset diagnostics.

E5.justification: Figure 8 newly reports convergence diagnostics over 20 independent observed datasets per setup, extending the single observed realization used in the retained diagnostics. The main coverage experiments still use 100 repetitions; confidence intervals and significance tests are not newly introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the original marginal-result tables retain their numerical results. Substantial new results appear in Tables 5–7 and Figures 7–9: semi-synthetic TabMGP coverage is 0.86 for Concrete and 0.98 for Phoneme, alternative baselines receive extensive result entries, and longer/repeated rollouts reveal both stabilization and failure cases.

T1.justification: The posterior definitions, martingale and a.c.i.d. conditions, Bayesian-recovery argument, predictive-training derivation, and credible-set formulas are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical correction is supplied; the added convergence discussion is interpretive.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central contribution and reliability claims. The conclusion now qualifies them with classification undercoverage and slow convergence, explicitly presenting TabMGP as a procedure that requires diagnostic checks.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantial applicability guidance concerning non-stabilizing finite rollouts, low-diversity datasets and ill-conditioned loss problems, and residual instability in skin and wine. It also removes v2's inference that skewed or multimodal densities demonstrate greater expressiveness. These changes materially qualify the interpretation of empirical reliability.

D1.justification: The code-release instructions change from anonymous hosting to a named GitHub repository. Appendix G documents the MLP architectures, activations, and binary-response threshold used for the new data generators. Existing TabPFN checkpoints, temperature, ensembles, hardware, and reported timings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4 sharpens the distinction between Nagler and Rügamer's conditional inference and TabMGP's unconditional loss-defined functionals, and adds criticism of copula bandwidth tuning. The cited-work inventory is retained; updated Fong–Yiu and Cui–Walker references correspond to existing works.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and narrative are retained, with sentence-level editing and clearer explanations of baselines and rollout length. New appendices are inserted before the retained density and marginal-coverage material, the appendix contents list is removed, and author and conference text is reformatted.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from one-column to two-column layout, relocating Figure 1 and compressing the main tables. Figure 6 is reorganized into regression and classification panels. Three new tables and three new figures are added, while existing density and marginal-coverage displays are retained and relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens scrutiny of the paper's central reliability claim. Longer and repeated-dataset diagnostics address v2's limited convergence checks, while alternative-prior and TabPFN-initialized copula comparisons address important baseline gaps. Reporting the resulting failures and applicability limits improves interpretation rather than merely adding favorable evidence. Finite-horizon diagnostics still do not establish a convergence guarantee.
